Director-level controls are AGE, TENURE, OTHER CEO (which equals 1 if
the director is the CEO of a public company), and OTHER DIRECTORSHIPS .
I expect OTHER DIRECTORSHIPS to have a positive coefficient because directors with more positions are likely to lose more than those with fewer
positions. Furthermore, directors that begin with zero positions cannot lose
any seats. <sup>16</sup> FIN EXPERT is included to examine whether the reputational
penalty varies for financial experts. DIRECTOR DEPARTURE allows me to
distinguish between directors who left the restating company board and
those who continued.


3. Sample


3.1 RESTATING COMPANY SAMPLE


The sample consists of firms that announced restatements from 1997 to
2001 as provided in Government Accounting Office (GAO) [2002]. <sup>17</sup> Table 2
explains the sample construction. The GAO database lists 794 companies,
of which 11 companies did not eventually restate, 74 are multiple restatements by the same company (I include them only once), and 32 are foreign
companies. I also drop companies for which I cannot collect the required
data for the three years following the restatement announcement: 81 companies without CRSP or Compustat data and 187 companies that stopped
filing proxy statements or 10-Ks (needed to collect director data) because
they delisted or merged.

16 I do not exclude these directors from the analysis because they can gain new directorships.
17 This database was created by the U.S. General Accounting Office as required by the
Sarbanes-Oxley Act. Please refer to GAO [2002] for details of the methodology used to create
the database.
